title: IT Threat Intel - IT Cybersecurity
description: Curated IT / enterprise cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_threatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: China-nexus Armory Castle has been exploiting a VMware vCenter authentication-bypass zero-day since September, hijacking single sign-on and creating admin accounts — CISA gives agencies until 23 November to patch
items.content_text: Broadcom’s advisory VMSA-2026-0009 fixes CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8), an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service component of vCenter. Mandiant and Google’s Threat Intelligence Group confirm that Armory Castle, the China-nexus group formerly tracked as UNC5221, has been exploiting it since early September, before any patch existed. Its BONESAW tool pulls data from vCenter, hijacks the single sign-on Security Token Service (SAML STS) and creates administrator accounts. The group paired it with the BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw CVE-2026-102764 (see that card), and ESET links its tooling to the Check Point gateway attacks (see that card). Fixed releases are vCenter 8.0 U3m and VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 5.2.5; vCenter 7.0 customers must contact Broadcom, and there is no workaround. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 November with a 23 November deadline (see that card). Control of vCenter means control of every virtual machine it manages. This leads over this week’s confirmed multi-organisation attacks, the N-able N-central mass exploitation (see that card), the ScreenConnect MSP campaign (see that card) and the Optimizely script injection (see that card), because vCenter is core infrastructure in a large share of enterprise data centres, the flaw was exploited for months before disclosure and the federal deadline is three days after listing. No victim organisations have been named.

_threatfeed.source_name: Broadcom VMSA-2026-0009; Rapid7; Mandiant / Google Threat Intelligence Group; CISA KEV via Security Affairs
_threatfeed.date_note: Exploited since early Sep 2026; advisory and Rapid7 analysis 19 Nov 2026; KEV 20 Nov 2026

items.title: N-able N-central “4EverAble2Shell” was exploited within hours of a public PoC: at least 21 production servers compromised, most already on the previous hotfix
items.content_text: A researcher, Sean Bales, published a proof of concept on 12 November for “4EverAble2Shell”, a chain that combines the Apache Axis flaw CVE-2026-90436 (see that card) with a bug in N-central’s Legacy API to give an unauthenticated attacker root on N-able’s remote-monitoring server. Exploitation started within hours. Huntback counted at least 21 production servers compromised, 19 of them already on Hotfix 2, in the US, Canada, South Africa, the UK, Germany, France and Sweden; attackers dropped the XMRig miner and a script from 157.20.241[.]16 (jup.sh). N-able confirmed attacks on customers that had not disabled the Legacy API and shipped 2026.4 HF3, which fixes 17 flaws (CVE-2026-129271 to -129287) and permanently blocks the Legacy APIs; every Agent and Probe must also be upgraded. So far the payload is a miner, but whoever controls an N-central server can push software to every client machine it manages.
tags: Incident — MSP / N-able N-central mass exploitation

items.title: Attackers are breaching MSPs through ScreenConnect and using its Run Command feature to plant rogue clients on customer machines; ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions across about 400 partners
items.content_text: Huntress saw a spike in attacks on ConnectWise ScreenConnect partners from 13 November. Counts are still moving: The Hacker News cites 205 hosts at 41 organisations, while BleepingComputer reports six MSPs, 286 endpoints and 47 organisations, and rising. The attackers misused ScreenConnect’s built-in Run Command feature to install their own rogue ScreenConnect clients, and persisted with a fake “Windows Update Agent” service, UpdateConnect.ClientService.exe. The suspected way in is an authentication flaw in a third-party RMM+ extension (versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32), which has no CVE. ConnectWise disabled five extensions, Labtech Plus, RMM Plus, RMM+ and two Password Link variants, across about 400 partner environments. A worm-like toolkit, SCKit, can also abuse ScreenConnect CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9, fixed in 26.6.5), though there is no evidence it was used here. The activity is unattributed and separate from October’s Storm-0940 case (see that card).

_threatfeed.source_name: Huntress; ConnectWise via The Hacker News; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Spike from 13 Nov 2026; ConnectWise action and reports 17 Nov 2026

items.title: Optimizely supply-chain attack injected malicious JavaScript into 178 organisations’ experiment scripts, loading on sites including Zoom, CNN, the BBC and Salesforce
items.content_text: Optimizely confirmed that attackers abused a flaw in the sign-up flow of its Optimizely Experimentation product to inject JavaScript into customers’ projects. Researcher Scott Helme found 188 infected files belonging to 178 organisations, and BleepingComputer confirmed the malicious code loading on sites including Zoom, CNN, the BBC, Salesforce, GitLab, KLM, American Eagle and Air France. The payload could skim payment cards, swap cryptocurrency addresses, steal cookies and take screenshots, and served iOS exploit kits. Optimizely fixed the flaw and removed the code on 16 November; Salesforce disabled Optimizely scripts on its sites. Because the code ran inside visitors’ browsers on the victims’ own domains, ordinary server-side monitoring would not have seen it, a week before the busiest online shopping period of the year.

items.title: Attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Gaia OS flaw to take root on Check Point gateways at about two dozen customers; some intrusions reached VMware ESXi and ran a wiper
items.content_text: Check Point says about two dozen customers were attacked through their security gateways. The attackers used the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, in KEV since 26 October, and then the Gaia OS privilege-escalation flaw CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8) to get root. A first wave on 30 October targeted Israeli organisations and a wider wave followed on 2 November. In some intrusions the attackers reached VMware ESXi hosts and ran a wiper, destroy_v6, leaving political, ransom-style notes. Check Point will not attribute the attacks; ESET says the tooling overlaps with the China-nexus group Armory Castle, the same group behind the vCenter zero-day (see the top story). CISA added the Gaia flaw to KEV on 13 November. It confirms that PHP2Shell, which this page led with in October, is now being used to compromise real organisations.
tags: Incident — Check Point gateways / PHP2Shell / wiper

items.title: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm attacks on third-party vendors; the n0n extortion group claims the data, and BleepingComputer reports cloud analytics firm Qubole is the suspected source
items.content_text: On 19 November all three firms confirmed that vendors had been attacked. JPMorgan Chase says attackers likely obtained marketing data held by a vendor, possibly including customer names and email addresses, and will contact affected customers. Visa says an Asia-Pacific provider was hit and no card numbers or Visa systems were involved. Mastercard says a provider exposed limited non-payment data for a subset of cardholders in a benefits programme and its network was not affected. The extortion group n0n claimed the data on 16 November; Reuters reviewed the leak and saw about 16,000 customer email addresses, some with phone numbers and postal codes, plus about 124 bank employee emails, which has not been verified. BleepingComputer reports that Qubole, a cloud data-analytics firm owned by Idera, is the suspected vendor; this is not confirmed and Qubole did not respond. n0n claims it used Qubole credentials between 14 and 26 October to reach customers’ AWS accounts, which matches research by Wiz and Sentra (see that card).

_threatfeed.date_note: n0n claim 16 Nov 2026; confirmations 19 Nov 2026; Qubole report 20 Nov 2026

items.title: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms attackers came in through a service provider’s platform and moved funds out of the bank’s own account; an outside estimate puts it at up to €118 million
items.content_text: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms that an attacker reached its network through a service provider’s platform and transferred funds from the bank’s own account, not from customer accounts, then converted them to cryptocurrency. The bank calls it a “sophisticated attack”, says customer assets are unaffected and that some of the funds were blocked. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT estimates the loss at up to €118 million (about $133 million); the bank confirms only the order of magnitude. No group has been named. The case shows how a trusted integration with payment rights can become a direct path to the money.
tags: Incident — Financial / theft via service provider

_threatfeed.category: Incident — Financial / theft via service provider
_threatfeed.source_name: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa statement; ZachXBT via BleepingComputer

items.title: The US Justice Department attributes the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance to North Korea’s TraderTraitor, and has moved to seize more than $1.2 billion
items.content_text: The Justice Department says North Korea’s TraderTraitor was behind the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance around 29 October; Binance puts the loss at about $6.3 billion and has set aside $6.34 billion. A court has authorised seizing or restraining more than $1.2 billion, part of more than $2.7 billion frozen so far. The DOJ also seized the cloud infrastructure behind “FaceStealer”, a scheme that used deepfake video calls and fake “technical issues” to trick targets into installing malware, linked to more than $400 million stolen over 18 months. A run of smaller crypto breaches has followed (see that card).
tags: Incident — Crypto / North Korea / law enforcement

_threatfeed.category: Incident — Crypto / North Korea / law enforcement
_threatfeed.source_name: US Department of Justice via The Block

items.title: N-able confirms attackers accessed a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud; portals, APIs and quarantine are offline while mail keeps flowing
items.content_text: N-able says attackers accessed one server in its hosted Mail Assure / SpamExperts email-filtering cloud, and that its investigation began on 16 November. Portals, APIs, quarantine and logging went offline in the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Europe, but as of 20 November mail was still being delivered and filtered. N-able says it has found no evidence that customer data or mailboxes were compromised, and that the incident is unrelated to the N-central attacks (see that card). MSPs that resell the service should keep their own customers informed.

_threatfeed.date_note: Investigation began 16 Nov 2026; confirmed 19 Nov 2026; status 20 Nov 2026

items.title: Vanderbilt University is restoring systems after a BYOD ransomware attack; the gang claims more than a million SSNs, and a class action has been filed
items.content_text: Vanderbilt University confirmed an “active cybersecurity incident” on 9 November affecting devices, systems and cloud services, and told people to shut down university devices and get off campus Wi-Fi. BleepingComputer saw the ransom note, README_BYOD_31.txt. The BYOD gang claims it encrypted databases and stole student, employee and research data including more than a million SSNs; that is not confirmed. By 10 November Wi-Fi, Okta, Outlook, Brightspace and Zoom were back; OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams stayed disabled, with OneDrive expected back in the first week of December; Box files were rolled back to before about 8:30am on 9 November and every password was reset. Full restoration will take several weeks. A proposed class action was filed in federal court in Tennessee on 17 November; a law professor says BYOD demanded $750,000, which is unconfirmed. This does not mean Vanderbilt University Medical Center was hit; it has not said so. BYOD has also hit Michigan State and UNM this autumn (see that card).

_threatfeed.date_note: Incident 9 Nov 2026; recovery update 10–13 Nov 2026; class action 17 Nov 2026

items.title: Bell Canada says an “agentic” attacker got into a pre-production Maximo environment and took enterprise customers’ contact details and some network IP addresses
items.content_text: Bell Canada confirmed on 17 November that an attacker reached a pre-production environment of its Maximo system, which it uses for circuit ordering and provisioning. The attacker took business contact details, ticket titles and some network-element IP addresses; Bell says no credentials or highly sensitive personal data were taken and has not given a count. Bell described the attacker as “agentic”, suggesting AI-driven tooling, but has not identified it. Bell is sharing indicators with enterprise customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security. Pre-production copies can hold real data under weaker controls.

items.title: Cursor confirms a breach that began with a key stored at Fireworks AI and led to a fake Claude Code extension on the marketplace cache it uses, reaching up to 5,000 users
items.content_text: Cursor says attackers used an access key stored at Fireworks AI to copy a Cursor storage bucket of historical agent traces. Some traces held API credentials that gave further access, and the attackers stole non-production source code, support data and customer contacts. On 29 October they placed a fake Anthropic Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, in the extension-marketplace cache Cursor uses; it was live for about 11 hours, may have reached up to 5,000 users and tried to install SSH backdoors. Anthropic’s real extension and Open VSX were not compromised. Wiz places it in a wider “Black October” campaign against AI developer platforms, including Railway (see that card), Fireworks AI and Notion. The attack is unattributed.
tags: Incident — AI developer platform / supply chain

_threatfeed.category: Incident — AI developer platform / supply chain
_threatfeed.date_note: Fake extension 29 Oct 2026; Cursor confirmation 14 Nov 2026

items.title: Railway says attackers broke out of build isolation, decrypted customer environment variables and ran up about $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage with stolen keys
items.content_text: Cloud platform Railway confirms attackers broke its build isolation from 20 October, took internal credentials and decrypted customer environment variables. Up to 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000 at most, may be affected, and tokens of 1,852 users were exposed, including GitHub OAuth tokens and AI provider keys. The stolen AI keys ran up about $740,000 in usage, which Railway says it will cover. It is part of the same “Black October” campaign as the Cursor breach (see that card).
tags: Incident — Cloud platform / AI keys abused

_threatfeed.category: Incident — Cloud platform / AI keys abused

items.title: Japanese furniture retailer Nitori says up to 37.62 million customer records may have leaked after an attacker sat in its systems from mid-October
items.content_text: Nitori found unauthorised access on 6 November and says the attacker had been inside since mid-October. Up to 37.62 million records may have leaked, covering names, contact details, dates of birth and order data from the Nitori Net online store and its marketplace stores. Nitori says passwords and card data were not involved. The cause is still under investigation and no group has claimed it. A dwell time of about three weeks before detection is the detail other retailers should take from this one.

items.title: Iris Ohyama’s Iris Plaza online store is offline after an outside cloud service was compromised; up to 7.7 million people may be affected
items.content_text: Iris Plaza, the online store of Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama, went offline after an unnamed external cloud service it uses was compromised; the breach was found on 28 October. Up to 7.7 million people may be affected: 5.8 million members, whose contact details, dates of birth and encrypted passwords were exposed, and 1.9 million guest buyers. No card data was involved. It is another case where the weak link was a service the retailer relied on rather than its own systems.

items.title: Online fashion retailer Revolve puts its breach at 1,515,073 people, including stored card numbers and expiry dates
items.content_text: Revolve told the Indiana attorney general that 1,515,073 people were affected. An intruder was inside its systems, including the e-commerce platform, from 11 September until the breach was found on 29 September; Revolve filed with the SEC on 29 October. Exposed data includes names, addresses and stored card numbers with expiry dates, possibly collected by “automated means”. No group has claimed it.

_threatfeed.source_name: Indiana AG filing and SEC filing via SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Intrusion 11–29 Sep 2026; SEC filing 29 Oct 2026; count reported 9 Nov 2026

items.title: Fandango confirms skimmer code on its checkout pages captured card numbers, CVVs and expiry dates for three days in October
items.content_text: Fandango says malicious code on its checkout pages captured card numbers, CVV codes, expiry dates, billing ZIP codes and email addresses between 8 and 11 October. It found the code on 30 October, removed it and is offering two years of monitoring; it has not said how many customers were affected. Together with the Optimizely injection (see that card), it shows checkout scripts are under attack right before Black Friday.

_threatfeed.date_note: Skimming 8–11 Oct 2026; found 30 Oct 2026; reported 16 Nov 2026

items.title: New Hampshire’s Monadnock Community Hospital is diverting ambulances and cancelling surgeries after a “cyber incident” took its network down
items.content_text: Monadnock Community Hospital, a 25-bed hospital in New Hampshire, has had a network outage since about 10 November. Elective surgeries and outpatient lab and radiology were cancelled and ambulances diverted. A 16 November notice says specialists confirmed a “cyber incident” that also affects its Jaffrey and Antrim sites, and some elective major surgeries are cancelled through 23 November. There is no restoration timeline, the data impact is under investigation and no group has claimed it.

items.title: A German district hospital in Greiz closed its emergency room after an extortion attack; police are following a lead on a suspect
items.content_text: The Greiz-Ronneburg district hospital in Thuringia, Germany, suffered a system failure on the evening of 14 November and its emergency room was out of service on 15 November. The district called it an “extortion attempt”, with a demand received on 15 November. The ER began reopening on 16 November. Police say they are following a lead on a suspect; no group has been named.

items.title: A cyberattack took down the West Virginia Legislature’s website and some IT systems from 19 November
items.content_text: The West Virginia Legislature’s website and some internal IT systems went down on 19 November and were still affected on 20 November. Officials say the incident is contained and limited to the Legislature, and that outside specialists are helping. They have neither confirmed nor denied ransomware, and no group has claimed it. The Record cites Comparitech’s count of 132 ransomware attacks on US government bodies in the third quarter, up 91% on a year earlier.

items.title: South Portland, Maine shut down its network after a security issue tied to cybercriminal activity; City Hall closed and the tax deadline moved
items.content_text: South Portland, Maine shut its network at about 11:30pm on 14 November after a security issue that, on preliminary findings, is tied to cybercriminal activity. Phones, in-person card payments, GIS, online portals and meeting streaming went down, and City Hall, the Assessing office and the library were closed through at least 19 November. The property-tax deadline was moved to 23 November. The city says most data was not compromised, and police, fire and EMS were unaffected.

items.title: DonorPerfect’s cyberattack cut off more than 11,000 nonprofits from donor records and payment forms for a week; GoFundMe Pro says donor data was taken through its Salesforce integration
items.content_text: DonorPerfect confirms a cyberattack: it saw anomalies in the week of 3 November, took access down on 10 November, began restoring on 14 November and had 99% of service back by 16 November. More than 11,000 nonprofit customers lost access to donor records and payment forms, and some switched to temporary PayPal pages. The company says it has a “high degree of confidence” data is safe while the investigation continues; the FBI is investigating. Its president described the attackers as “AI bots”, her own characterisation. In the same report, GoFundMe Pro says an unauthorised party made repeated access attempts and obtained personal donor and supporter information through its Salesforce integration, possibly including Salesforce credentials; transactions were not disrupted and no counts were given. DonorPerfect’s president says two other platform CEOs told her privately they had been attacked, which is unconfirmed. Giving Tuesday is 1 December.

_threatfeed.source_name: DonorPerfect; GoFundMe Pro via The Chronicle of Philanthropy
_threatfeed.date_note: Anomalies week of 3 Nov 2026; restoration 14–16 Nov 2026; reported 17–18 Nov 2026

items.title: Central Ohio Primary Care reports 1,351,650 people affected by an August breach that started with a voice-phishing call
items.content_text: Central Ohio Primary Care’s filing with the HHS Office for Civil Rights lists 1,351,650 people affected. In August a voice-phishing call led to credential theft; access was blocked on 25 August. Exposed data includes names, addresses, Social Security numbers and financial and health information. HIPAA Journal says the attacker “appears to be” the Chaos ransomware group, which is an inference, not a confirmation. It was the second-largest healthcare breach reported to HHS in October (see that card).

_threatfeed.source_name: HHS OCR breach portal via HIPAA Journal

items.title: Women’s-health EHR vendor Dorsata says an attacker used a then-unknown Metabase flaw to reach 58,249 patients’ records at partner providers
items.content_text: Dorsata, which supplies EHR and data tools for women’s health practices, says an attacker exploited a then-unknown flaw in the open-source Metabase analytics tool between 10 and 12 August and reached partner providers’ data on 58,249 patients, including names, dates of birth, vital signs, medications, vaccinations, insurance and medical histories. The flaw has been patched. Threat-intel firm VenariX says the Dire Wolf group appears to have used the same flaw in at least two later attacks, which is unconfirmed.

items.title: Law firms Baker McKenzie and Troutman Pepper Locke disclose social-engineering breaches affecting about 89,000 people combined
items.content_text: Texas filings show Baker McKenzie notified 25,837 people and Troutman Pepper Locke 63,358, about 89,000 in total. Baker McKenzie staff were socially engineered on 14 and 17 August, exposing SSNs and medical information. At Troutman, an employee sent documents to an unauthorised person on 7 August, exposing names and SSNs. Both firms say there was no wider access to their systems, both offer 24 months of monitoring, no attacker has been named and the cases are not linked.

_threatfeed.source_name: Texas AG filings via eSecurity Planet

items.title: A run of smaller crypto breaches followed Binance: Mercado Bitcoin, BitMart, BTCPay Server hot wallets, Gnosis Pay, SignalPlus and Unocoin
items.content_text: Blockhead tallies a series of breaches in early November. Mercado Bitcoin lost an estimated $49 million on 2 November, about $11 million of it frozen; BitMart lost about $391,000 the same day; hot wallets on BTCPay Server 2.4.1 and earlier were swept on 1 November; Gnosis Pay exposed data from a legacy card system on 3 November; SignalPlus was hit on 5 November through a compromised vendor Telegram account and a fake Microsoft Teams invite; and Unocoin reported unauthorised server access between 6 and 12 November. The common thread is people and vendors, not novel exploits.

items.title: University Hospitals in Cleveland has brought MyChart back after two weeks offline, which it calls the sign that it has recovered; some features remain degraded
items.content_text: University Hospitals (UH), a 21-hospital system in northeast Ohio, found unusual server activity on 22 October and disconnected its systems from the internet. For two weeks MyChart, video visits, parts of e-prescribing and data exchange with outside systems were down and some procedures were rescheduled. On 7 November UH brought MyChart back online and called it “the sign that UH has recovered”, while warning that some features would be degraded as data is reconciled. UH has not reported ransomware or data theft, and no group has claimed the attack. The incident is a useful benchmark: about two weeks from disconnection to patient-portal recovery.

items.title: BYOD claims data on 1.3 million Michigan State students; MSU confirmed suspicious activity in October and forced a NetID password reset
items.content_text: The BYOD gang claimed on 1 November that it holds data on 1.3 million current and former Michigan State University students; that is not verified. MSU confirmed “suspicious cyber activity” in early October involving a potential credential compromise, forced every NetID password to be reset on 1 October with a 15-character minimum, and says it has no evidence its central Active Directory was compromised.

_threatfeed.date_note: Activity early Oct 2026; claim 1 Nov 2026; reported 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Richmond Public Schools is rebuilding its network from backups after an October attack took the whole district offline; a forensic audit is under way
items.content_text: Richmond Public Schools in Virginia, with more than 22,000 students, is still rebuilding after an October attack took the entire district offline. Leaders say data accessed in the attack may be on the dark web, which has not been confirmed. A forensic audit is under way, the district is running on a temporary network, Chromebooks have been moved to a clean server, systems are being rebuilt from backups and all passwords have been reset. The rebuild is the kind of event the national K-12 survey shows most districts are not staffed for (see that card).

items.title: BYOD ransomware hit UNM Health Sciences Center, diverting ambulances for two hours; UNM made no concessions, and BYOD later offered free decryption keys while keeping the data
items.content_text: A BYOD ransomware attack on the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center on 26 October diverted ambulances from UNM Hospital between 12:30 and 2:30pm, cancelled outpatient surgeries and appointments and cancelled classes through 27 October. UNM says end-user devices were affected, not core systems or servers, and that it was fully open again by 27–28 October; it made no concessions to the attackers. BYOD claims 36,000 machines and patient, student, payroll and SSN data, which is unconfirmed; the FBI is investigating. Paubox and The Record report BYOD later “apologised” and offered free decryption keys while still holding the data. The same gang has since hit Vanderbilt (see that card).
tags: Incident — Healthcare and education / BYOD ransomware

_threatfeed.category: Incident — Healthcare and education / BYOD ransomware
_threatfeed.source_name: Medical Daily; GovTech; Paubox; The Record

items.title: University of Copenhagen: an intrusion exposed national ID numbers for about 525,000 people and campus door PINs for about 20,000 — administrative systems stay shut as a precaution
items.content_text: The University of Copenhagen says attackers it detected on 20 October reached data on about 525,000 people, including full names, Danish national identity (CPR) numbers, phone numbers and personal email addresses, and compromised the ID-card PIN codes of about 20,000 staff and students. The PINs have been reissued and the restricted areas reopened, and the university is notifying people by letter through Digital Post. On 26 October it shut down administrative systems including WorkZone and Nimbus after what it first called a new attack; on 27 October it said that activity was linked to the original intrusion, not a second breach. Incoming network traffic is blocked, so staff need VPN or on-campus access, and the university says the systems it closed were not compromised. It has reported the breach to the Danish Data Protection Agency; no group has claimed it.

_threatfeed.source_name: University of Copenhagen; BleepingComputer; Infosecurity Magazine
_threatfeed.date_note: Detected 20 Oct 2026; PIN update 25 Oct 2026; shutdown 26 Oct 2026; update 27 Oct 2026

items.title: Microsoft says China-aligned Storm-0940 took over ConnectWise Cloud Backup’s app identities and used them to sign in to customers’ Microsoft 365 tenants — several reached privileged access, and ConnectWise is restoring services in phases
items.content_text: Microsoft said on 21 October that it assesses a China-state aligned actor it tracks as Storm-0940 was behind the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise. The attacker gained control of the identities of several ConnectWise cloud applications tied to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) and used them to sign in to customers’ Microsoft 365 tenants as the application, so multi-factor authentication never applied. Microsoft says more than 2,250 tenants received sign-in attempts, which are attempts rather than compromises; most failed, but several reached privileged cloud access, some in under three hours, followed by directory reconnaissance, new app credentials and role changes. Huntress saw unauthorized sign-ins at 162 tenants it monitors. Storm-0940 used ARTEX, an open-source penetration-testing framework that can use any AI model; Microsoft does not attribute the earlier ARTEX intrusions at Korean financial firms to Storm-0940. ConnectWise first detected the activity on 14 October, suspended Cloud Backup and shut its SaaS Security and Cloud Management services; its CEO said on 22 October that restoration is proceeding in controlled phases and that customers should keep the connections disabled until ConnectWise contacts them. ConnectWise says it has no evidence partner backup data was compromised. This page found no later ConnectWise statement it could verify. The November attacks on ScreenConnect partners are a separate, unattributed campaign (see that card).

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Threat Intelligence; ConnectWise via Cybersecurity Dive and CyberScoop; Huntress via BleepingComputer; The Record
_threatfeed.date_note: Activity first detected 14 Oct 2026; Microsoft attribution 21 Oct 2026; CEO restoration statement 22 Oct 2026

items.title: Australian supermarket chain Coles confirms a “cyber security incident” but says stores, online shopping and Flybuys are unaffected
items.content_text: Coles says it is responding to a cyber security incident with outside experts and the Australian Cyber Security Centre. So far it has found no evidence that customer, staff or supplier data was compromised, and stores, online shopping and the Flybuys loyalty programme are working normally. No group has claimed the attack and Coles has not said what happened.

items.title: StubHub International warns customers that names, emails and phone numbers may have been exposed after unauthorised access in late October and early November
items.content_text: StubHub International, operated by Ticketbis S.L., says an unauthorised party accessed its systems between late October and early November. Names, email addresses, phone numbers and region settings may have been exposed. StubHub says it has no evidence that passwords, banking details or card data were involved, and has not said how many customers are affected.

_threatfeed.date_note: Access late Oct–early Nov 2026; reported 18 Nov 2026

items.title: York University in Toronto confirms theft of web-form data from 14 university sites, some going back to 2007 and including government ID and health information
items.content_text: York University says attackers stole data submitted through web forms on 14 of its sites, covering submissions from 2007 to 2026. Depending on the form, the data includes contact details, York IDs, government ID, health and financial information, criminal-background information and photos. The breach was found on 25 October. York has not given a count and no group has claimed it. Old forms that kept collecting and storing sensitive data for nearly two decades are the real lesson.

items.title: Two groups claim AARP: n0n posts what it calls a “membership audience” dataset, and The Gentlemen reportedly claimed it a day later — AARP has not commented
items.content_text: The n0n group claimed AARP on 16 November, marking it “NOT PAID — EXPOSED” and listing what it calls a “membership audience” dataset dated September 2026, with several other datasets dated 2022–23. AARP has made no statement. Bitdefender and SOCRadar both say n0n inflates its claims (see that card). ClassAction.org, citing Ransomware.live and HookPhish, says The Gentlemen also claimed AARP around 17 November, which conflicts with n0n’s claim. A law firm is investigating a class action. None of the record counts in circulation has been verified.

items.title: The Gentlemen ransomware group lists NVIDIA with a 28 November countdown but no proof; NVIDIA says its own systems show no sign of compromise and it is looking at a third-party partner
items.content_text: The Gentlemen, which Microsoft tracks as Storm-2697, listed NVIDIA on its leak site with a countdown to 28 November and posted no proof; this is a claim only. NVIDIA says it has seen no sign that its own systems or networks were affected, and that it is investigating an incident that “may have affected a third-party partner”. If data does appear, it is more likely to come from that partner than from NVIDIA itself, which is a pattern repeated across this page.

items.title: Wiz and Sentra: an attacker used Qubole’s own AWS account to assume roles in customers’ accounts, reading secrets and copying S3 data
items.content_text: Wiz and Sentra report that between 14 and 26 October an attacker used credentials for Qubole’s own AWS account to assume IAM roles in customer accounts that trusted Qubole, most of which were no longer in use. From there the attacker read Lambda environment variables, Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store entries and copied S3 data, exposing AWS keys, Entra ID client secrets and Okta client credentials. The activity is unattributed. It is the same period n0n names in its claim about the Chase, Visa and Mastercard vendor data (see that card). The lesson applies to any SaaS vendor you once granted a cross-account role: the trust stays until you remove it.
tags: Threat intel — Cloud supply chain / AWS cross-account trust

_threatfeed.category: Threat intel — Cloud supply chain / AWS cross-account trust
_threatfeed.source_name: Wiz; Sentra via The Hacker News

items.title: Google’s threat group says attacker use of agentic AI has “crossed a significant threshold”, with automated patch-diff-to-exploit pipelines and multi-agent pentest frameworks in live intrusions
items.content_text: Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reports that multi-agent penetration-testing frameworks, including CAIRN, HexStrike AI and PentAGI, are being used in real intrusions, and describes a fully automated “exploit_agent” pipeline that compares patches, writes exploits and runs them. Zero-days exploited averaged 11 a month in 2026, against 8 in 2025, with a spike of 22 in August. North Korea’s MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE altered AI coding-assistant configuration files in internal repositories to deliver a backdoor. GTIG says these tools “trade stealth for velocity”: they are fast but noisy, which gives defenders who watch for bursts of activity a chance to catch them.

items.title: Two trojanized releases of Microsoft’s agent-framework package were live on PyPI for about 45 minutes, stealing cloud, CI and developer credentials on Python start-up
items.content_text: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft’s agent-framework Python package were published on 17 November and stayed live for about 45 minutes before PyPI quarantined them; 1.26.0 is clean. They installed a .pth file, af_runtime_diag.pth, which runs every time Python starts and steals environment secrets, .env files, Azure, pip, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face credentials, and Azure managed-identity and DevOps OIDC tokens; 1.26.2 also stole GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Data went to webhook.site. The releases were published with valid credentials, and how those were obtained is not known.

items.title: LLMjacking is costing victims up to $1 million in AI charges, Google says, with stolen keys resold through “LLM mixers” handling more than 1,000 requests a second
items.content_text: Google’s threat group and Mandiant describe two LLMjacking clusters: one scans for exposed LLM endpoints, the other steals API keys. Access is resold through “LLM mixers” that handle more than 1,000 requests a second, and a group tracked as UNC6993 aggregates and sells keys. Victims have been billed up to $1 million, some more than $100,000 in a single day. The actors exploited LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217, now in KEV (see that card). The Hacker News lists financial, retail, transportation and technology firms among the targets.
tags: Threat intel — LLMjacking / stolen AI keys

_threatfeed.category: Threat intel — LLMjacking / stolen AI keys
_threatfeed.source_name: Google GTIG / Mandiant via BleepingComputer; The Hacker News

items.title: Enea identifies “SilentAir”, a state-level actor rerouting calls and SMS, including 2FA codes, through hijacked operator nodes in at least six Asian countries
items.content_text: Telecom security firm Enea says a newly identified actor, SilentAir, which it assesses with high confidence to be state-level, uses hijacked nodes at operators in at least six Asian countries to reroute targets’ calls and text messages, including two-factor codes, over SS7 and Diameter signalling. Taiwan is the main target, particularly political and government figures. Enea links it to China only with low confidence. It also reports that Liminal Panda’s GTPDoor implant is exploiting IPX roaming links, with an estimated 5 to 10 or more operators infected. SMS codes are not a safe second factor for people a state wants to watch.
tags: Threat intel — Telecom signalling / SMS interception

_threatfeed.category: Threat intel — Telecom signalling / SMS interception

items.title: ESET: Russia’s Turla uses a new .NET “Cereal” framework that turns a compromised Exchange server into its own command channel; Romania’s SRI confirms a related intrusion
items.content_text: ESET says Turla used a new eight-part .NET framework it calls Cereal against government bodies in Kazakhstan and Romania in late 2025. The framework uses the compromised Exchange server itself as command-and-control, and its CerealBox module injects into EdgeTransport.exe to filter and exfiltrate emails carrying DOC, DOCX and PDF attachments; the Romanian copy was set to collect NATO and EU correspondence. On 16 November Romania’s SRI intelligence service said Turla got into an unnamed government institution in December 2025 through Microsoft software flaws to intercept NATO and EU email; it says the intrusion was contained and it found no evidence of sensitive data theft. Russia denies involvement.

_threatfeed.source_name: ESET via The Hacker News; Romania SRI via The Record
_threatfeed.date_note: Campaign late 2025; ESET report 10 Nov 2026; SRI statement 16 Nov 2026

items.title: KnowBe4: Black Friday and holiday-sale phishing rose 165% in the first week of November, mostly luxury-goods lures leading to fake stores
items.content_text: KnowBe4 says holiday-sale phishing rose 103% in October over September and 165% in the first week of November; its Defend product saw a 260% week-on-week jump. About 94% of lures use luxury goods and lead to fake stores that collect card details. Industrial and infrastructure organisations received 25% of the lures, and public sector, education and nonprofit organisations 21.2%, so this is not only a consumer problem: employees shop from work accounts and devices.

items.title: Bitdefender counts 1,072 claimed ransomware victims in October, but says n0n has only about 20 real victims behind its 126 claims
items.content_text: Bitdefender’s monthly debrief counts 1,072 ransomware victims claimed on leak sites in October, or 946 without n0n’s 126 claims. The most active groups were n0n, The Gentlemen, Qilin, Akira and Booba Team, and more than 17 new groups appeared in two months. Bitdefender says with high confidence that n0n has only about 20 real victims. It also describes a former Gentlemen affiliate, Azazel, using the Model Context Protocol to connect an AI coding assistant to a reverse shell. Leak-site counts measure claims, not confirmed breaches.

items.title: Healthcare breaches reported to HHS in October affected 10.1 million people, led by iRhythm Technologies at 8.2 million
items.content_text: Paubox’s count of reports to the HHS Office for Civil Rights shows 34 healthcare breaches in October affecting 10,116,362 people. The largest was iRhythm Technologies, at 8,179,772, followed by Central Ohio Primary Care at 1,351,650 (see that card). Two reports account for most of the month’s total, which is typical: a single large vendor breach can outweigh dozens of smaller ones.

items.title: More than half of US K-12 schools had a cyber incident last year, a CIS, MS-ISAC and CoSN report finds, and only 15% test their response plans
items.content_text: The report says 51% of K-12 schools had at least one cyber incident in the past year and 34% suffered disruption, with more than 11,600 escalated incidents in 2025–26. Phishing is the top concern for 87%. Most (83%) have MFA, but only 59% have an incident-response plan and 15% test it. MS-ISAC notified 808 K-12 organisations about exposed credentials. EdTech Magazine reports two-thirds of districts have security teams of one or two people. Richmond Public Schools’ rebuild shows the cost (see that card).

_threatfeed.source_name: CIS / MS-ISAC / CoSN via Route Fifty

items.title: CISA, the FBI and UK and German partners say SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organisations since August 2024 — exposed VPN logins and old edge-device flaws are the way in
items.content_text: Joint advisory AA26-293A, released on 20 October by CISA, the FBI and the US Secret Service with Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, says SafePay has hit at least 600 organisations in multiple critical-infrastructure sectors across the Americas, Europe and Australia since August 2024. SafePay is a closed group with no affiliates that steals data before encrypting it. The agencies list exposed or brute-forced credentials, VPN logins (notably from Mullvad addresses), phished accounts and automated exploitation of edge devices, including the Cisco ASA and Firepower Threat Defense flaws CVE-2020-3259 and CVE-2023-20269. Inside, the operators use WinRM, PsExec and RDP, move data with tools such as FileZilla, WinSCP and Rclone, delete shadow copies and reset NAS devices that hold backups. The advisory names no victims; SafePay claimed the Conduent breach disclosed in January 2025, and Conduent agreed on 16 October to an $80 million class settlement. On 22 October the American Hospital Association flagged the advisory to hospitals, the development this card is dated to.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA / FBI joint advisory AA26-293A via BleepingComputer and Cybersecurity Dive; HIPAA Journal; Conduent Form 8-K
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory 20 Oct 2026; reported 21 Oct 2026; Conduent settlement 16 Oct 2026

items.title: Huntress: unpatched GeoVision camera software was used to run a miner as SYSTEM on 13 organisations’ networks, with a vulnerable driver to tamper with Defender; Fortinet tracks a separate SQL Server brute-force campaign
items.content_text: Huntress saw attackers abuse unpatched GeoVision camera-management software on 13 organisations’ networks between 8 and 10 November, running the XMRig miner as SYSTEM through GeoStartupAgentService.exe and loading the vulnerable driver wsftprm.sys to tamper with Microsoft Defender. Separately, Fortinet reports a brute-force campaign running since early October against internet-facing Microsoft SQL Server instances that uses T-SQL to deliver XMRig and the Gh0st RAT. Neither is sophisticated; both rely on forgotten software and exposed services.
tags: Threat intel — Unpatched software abused for mining

_threatfeed.category: Threat intel — Unpatched software abused for mining
_threatfeed.source_name: Huntress; Fortinet via The Hacker News weekly recap

items.title: Swarm’s bee-js npm package and Swarm Desktop were briefly backdoored to steal wallet keys and plant a hidden ScreenConnect client
items.content_text: Version 13.3.0 of the npm package @ethersphere/bee-js was live for about 75 minutes with roughly 10 downloads, and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 was downloaded 65 times, after attackers abused a bot account and maintainer accounts. The malicious versions stole wallet keys, installed a Go shell called evjawbreaker and, on Windows, a hidden ScreenConnect client running as SYSTEM. Socket links the activity to the SleepyDuck campaign. The download numbers are small, but the hidden remote-access client is the same technique seen in the MSP attacks (see that card).

items.title: CISA added four exploited flaws to KEV on 20 November with a 23 November deadline: Cisco Expressway, VMware vCenter, Apache Roller and an older SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal bug
items.content_text: On 20 November CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, all with a 23 November due date for federal civilian agencies: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8; see that card), VMware vCenter CVE-2026-123890 (9.8; the top story above), Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 (9.8; see that card) and SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal CVE-2025-42884, a JNDI injection flaw rated 6.5 that SAP fixed in November 2025. CISA confirms exploitation of the SAP flaw but no public details of the attacks have been released. A three-day window is now the norm for this catalog rather than the exception, so the practical message is to treat a KEV listing as a same-week change, not a monthly-cycle item.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog via The Hacker News; Security Affairs

items.title: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 lets an unauthenticated attacker reach root on clustered nodes; F6 found two internet-facing nodes breached at a Russian organisation, and CISA set a 23 November deadline
items.content_text: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) combines hard-coded credentials with weak certificate validation in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, giving an unauthenticated attacker a root-level RPC channel. Cisco disclosed it on 21 October and fixed it in X15.5.20; there is no workaround, and customers on X14 must move to a fixed X15 release. Russian security firm F6 describes an intrusion in which two internet-facing Expressway nodes running X15.5.3 at a Russian organisation were breached and the attacker moved laterally to internal cluster nodes, using Python scripts that F6 says may have been written with AI help. SecurityWeek reports exploitation began soon after a public proof of concept appeared. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 November with a 23 November deadline. Expressway is widely used to bridge video and voice calling to the internet, which makes it an edge device in many government and telecom networks.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco advisory; F6 research via SecurityWeek; CISA KEV
_threatfeed.date_note: Disclosed 21 Oct 2026; KEV 20 Nov 2026; reported 21 Nov 2026

items.title: Apache Roller pre-auth RCE CVE-2026-129448 is being exploited, and turning off XML-RPC does not block it — upgrade to 6.1.7
items.content_text: Apache says CVE-2026-129448, a deserialization flaw in the XML-RPC handling of the Roller blog server, lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and on 17 November said it “is being actively exploited”. It is rated CVSS 9.8. Apache warns that disabling XML-RPC in Roller’s settings does not remove the exposure. The fix is in 6.1.6 and later, with 6.1.7 recommended. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 November with a 23 November deadline. Roller is a niche product, so it does not lead this page, but it still runs on university, research and corporate blog sites that are often forgotten in patch inventories.

_threatfeed.source_name: Apache Software Foundation advisory via SecurityWeek; CISA KEV
_threatfeed.date_note: Apache exploitation notice 17 Nov 2026; KEV 20 Nov 2026

items.title: Apache Axis 1.x flaw CVE-2026-90436 is being used against Confluence Data Center: Rapid7 watched an attacker go from the wiki to a cloud data warehouse in about four hours
items.content_text: CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8) is a remote-code-execution flaw in Apache Axis 1.x, a long-retired web-services library that is still embedded in commercial products; Apache issued only a patch commit when it was disclosed on 6 November. Rapid7 saw it exploited on 13 November against an Atlassian Confluence Data Center server with the Remote API enabled: the attacker ran hundreds of commands and database queries, hunted for credentials and card data, reached a cloud data warehouse in about four hours and signed in to Microsoft 365 with a service account about 12 hours in. A Metasploit module followed on 17 November, and Previdian logged 50 attempts from 14 IP addresses between 12 and 19 November. The same flaw is half of the N-central “4EverAble2Shell” chain (see that card). Fixes are Confluence 9.2.28 (9 November) or 10.x and N-central 2026.4 HF3. CISA added it to KEV on 18 November with a 21 November deadline, which has now passed.

_threatfeed.source_name: Rapid7; Atlassian; Previdian; CISA KEV via SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Disclosed 6 Nov 2026; exploited 13 Nov 2026; Metasploit 17 Nov 2026; KEV 18 Nov 2026

items.title: CISA’s 18 November KEV batch: REDCap research-survey RCE with web shells and miners, LiteLLM tied to LLMjacking, Synology DSM tied to C3RB3R ransomware, and Apache Axis
items.content_text: CISA added four exploited flaws on 18 November. Vanderbilt REDCap CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS 9.8) is a code-injection RCE in the research-survey platform used across universities and hospitals; Safe Security saw a web shell and the XMRig miner dropped, and an attacker needs a valid public survey hash. LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 (8.8) is an RCE in the /guardrails/test_custom_code endpoint of the AI-gateway software; Google’s threat group links it to LLMjacking (see that card). Synology DSM CVE-2024-10441 (9.8) is being used by C3RB3R ransomware (see that card), and Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 has its own card (see that card). DSM, REDCap and Axis were due 21 November; LiteLLM is due 2 December.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog via The Hacker News; Safe Security; Google Threat Intelligence Group

items.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support CVE-2026-102764 is part of the Armory Castle campaign that also hit vCenter, Google’s threat group says — exploited since 29 August
items.content_text: CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4 9.3) is an authentication bypass in BeyondTrust Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier, fixed by patch BT26-05-RS. Rapid7 reports it has been exploited since 29 August by Armory Castle, the China-nexus group formerly tracked as UNC5221, which deployed the SAWFLY web shell and the BARECLAW tunneller. CISA added it to KEV on 16 October. On 20–21 November Google’s threat group tied it to the same group’s vCenter zero-day campaign, where the two flaws were used together (see the top story). Remote-support tools give attackers ready-made, trusted access to every endpoint they manage.
tags: Advisory — BeyondTrust Remote Support / Armory Castle

_threatfeed.category: Advisory — BeyondTrust Remote Support / Armory Castle
_threatfeed.source_name: Rapid7; Google Threat Intelligence Group; CISA KEV
_threatfeed.date_note: Exploited since 29 Aug 2026; KEV 16 Oct 2026; Rapid7 update 2 Nov 2026; GTIG link 20–21 Nov 2026

items.title: Microsoft’s November Patch Tuesday is enormous — more than 1,000 fixes, one exploited Outlook zero-day, and critical LDAP, Windows Search and Exchange flaws to prioritise
items.content_text: Microsoft’s 10 November release is very large: IT-Connect counts 1,093 fixes excluding Edge, with 63 rated Critical, while The Hacker News counts 1,259. One flaw is exploited, the Outlook spoofing zero-day CVE-2026-124194 (see that card). The ones to move up the queue are Windows LDAP RCE CVE-2026-119958 (9.8), Windows Search RCE CVE-2026-116928 (9.8), which can be reached through an Exchange attachment, Schannel RCE CVE-2026-119952 (8.1), Active Directory Domain Services flaws CVE-2026-118146 (8.8) and CVE-2026-118148 (7.5), both marked “exploitation more likely”, Outlook preview-pane RCEs CVE-2026-110043, -110068 and -111309 (8.8) and Exchange RCE CVE-2026-118207 (8.8). With volume this high, ranking by exposure matters more than ever.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Security Update Guide via IT-Connect; The Hacker News

items.title: Exploited Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194 leaks NTLMv2 hashes when a user opens a crafted message file — update Office and block outbound SMB
items.content_text: Microsoft confirms exploitation of CVE-2026-124194 (CVSS 6.5), a spoofing flaw in which opening a crafted message file makes Outlook connect to an outside server without the usual external-content warning, sending the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The Preview Pane is not an attack vector, so a user has to open the file. Microsoft has not named an actor. Fixed builds are 16.0.14334.21048 and 16.0.17932.21140. CISA added it to KEV on 10 November with a 24 November deadline. Leaked NTLM hashes can be cracked or relayed to other services, so the score understates the risk for organisations that still allow NTLM internally; law firms, government offices and banks that receive lots of outside mail are the likeliest targets.

items.title: Chrome’s eighth exploited zero-day of 2026, CVE-2026-125350, is a use-after-free in XML handling — update to 157.0.8103.50/.51
items.content_text: Google says it is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free in Chrome’s XML component rated CVSS 8.8, exists in the wild. It is the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited this year. The fix is in Chrome 157.0.8103.50 and .51. CISA added it to KEV on 10 November with a 24 November deadline. Other Chromium-based browsers, including Microsoft Edge, Brave and Opera, need their own updates once their vendors ship the fix.

_threatfeed.source_name: Google Chrome Releases via The Hacker News; CISA KEV

items.title: Barracuda confirms two Email Security Gateway flaws were chained to root against a small number of organisations; watchTowr has published an exploit
items.content_text: Barracuda says attackers chained CVE-2026-116606, an authentication weakness that lets an attacker restore a crafted configuration, with CVE-2026-111560, an OS command injection in the timezone field, to gain root on its Email Security Gateway. Barracuda confirmed exploitation against a “small number” of organisations. The command-injection flaw also affects Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF, WAF Control Center and Web Security Gateway. The attacker needs access to the admin interface. Sources disagree on the CVSS scores, so this page only describes the chain as critical. Patches BNSF-40425 and BNSF-40430 fix it, and watchTowr has published a working exploit. CISA’s deadline was 13 November.
tags: Advisory — Barracuda ESG / chained to root

_threatfeed.category: Advisory — Barracuda ESG / chained to root
_threatfeed.source_name: Barracuda advisory; watchTowr; CISA KEV via BleepingComputer

items.title: CISA’s 9 November KEV batch gave agencies three days to fix OpenSSH “SSHole”, GPUStack, SignalWire FreeSWITCH and IBM Aspera Faspex
items.content_text: CISA added four exploited flaws on 9 November, all due 12 November: OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 (“SSHole”, CVSS 8.1; see that card), GPUStack CVE-2026-102895 (9.8), an open-source manager for GPU clusters that serve AI models; SignalWire FreeSWITCH CVE-2026-116779 (9.8), the telephony engine inside many VoIP and contact-centre platforms; and IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2026-123218 (9.8), a large-file transfer server used by media, healthcare and legal teams to exchange big files with outsiders. Faspex servers usually face the internet, so give them the same urgency as an edge VPN. The deadline has passed.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog via The Hacker News

items.title: OpenSSH “SSHole” CVE-2026-123158 lets attackers log in to accounts with a “*” password field on Alpine-style systems — GreyNoise and watchTowr have seen it used
items.content_text: CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS 8.1) makes sshd accept a password for accounts whose password field is *, which normally means “no password login”. It only affects OpenSSH older than 10.6p2 built on musl libc, as on Alpine Linux, without PAM and with password authentication turned on; glibc-based distributions are not affected. Fixes shipped in OpenSSH 10.6p2 and Alpine packages on 5 November, and sshd must be restarted. GreyNoise saw post-exploitation activity from six IP addresses across 18 attack chains, with one actor, “GT10”, deploying a TAC Agent command-and-control implant; watchTowr saw botnets and miners; Defused calls it small-scale. CISA’s deadline was 12 November. The exposure is concentrated in containers and appliances built on Alpine.

_threatfeed.source_name: OX Security; GreyNoise; watchTowr; Defused; CISA KEV

items.title: Cisco BroadWorks XXE CVE-2026-20320 is in KEV; Malbear Labs claims an AI-driven “Operation Snowball” used it against a European telecom and 13 companies hosted on it
items.content_text: CISA added Cisco BroadWorks blind XXE CVE-2026-20320 (CVSS 7.5, fixed in August) to KEV on 10 November with a 24 November deadline, together with Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder CVE-2026-111793 (4.3, fixed 1.1.22.0). Malbear Labs claims an unknown Chinese-speaking actor used an autonomous attack framework running on a jailbroken DeepSeek model against a European telecom operator and 13 companies hosted on its BroadWorks platform, stealing credentials, billing and subscriber records and the BroadWorks XSP private key, and using Sliver, Chisel and Behinder. Cisco and the operator have not confirmed those details. BroadWorks runs the hosted voice services that many carriers resell to businesses, so a stolen XSP key matters to their customers too.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV; Malbear Labs via The Hacker News

items.title: Ivanti patches two more Connect Secure zero-days chained with a KEV-listed flaw since at least 1 October; Volexity says UTA0576 tampers with logs and evades the Integrity Checker
items.content_text: Ivanti has fixed two more Connect Secure zero-days, a privilege-escalation flaw CVE-2026-111357 and an authenticated file-upload flaw CVE-2026-118527, which attackers chained with the KEV-listed CVE-2026-104935 since at least 1 October. Volexity attributes the activity to a cluster it tracks as UTA0576: the actor uses no malware, re-exploits the device for every command, tampers with logs and evades Ivanti’s Integrity Checker Tool, so a clean check is not proof of a clean appliance. Shadowserver counts more than 5,000 exposed Connect Secure devices. VPN gateways remain the most direct route into government and financial networks.
tags: Advisory — Ivanti Connect Secure / zero-day chain

_threatfeed.category: Advisory — Ivanti Connect Secure / zero-day chain
_threatfeed.date_note: Exploited since 1 Oct 2026; fixes and report 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Synology warns C3RB3R ransomware is hitting NAS devices running outdated DSM; Shadowserver counts more than 380,000 Synology NAS exposed to the internet
items.content_text: Synology says the C3RB3R ransomware is attacking NAS devices that run outdated DiskStation Manager builds, using the flaws in its advisory SA_24_20: CVE-2024-10441, CVE-2024-50629 and CVE-2024-10445. Encrypted files get a .L0CK3D extension and a read-me3.txt note. Fixed builds are DSM 7.2.2-72806-1, 7.2.1-69057-6, 7.2-64570-4, 7.1.1-42962-7 and 6.2.4-25556-8. Shadowserver sees more than 380,000 Synology NAS devices reachable from the internet. CISA added CVE-2024-10441 to KEV on 18 November. Small offices, schools, law firms and nonprofits often keep file shares and backups on exactly these boxes, which is why a two-year-old flaw is still paying off for attackers.

_threatfeed.source_name: Synology advisory SA_24_20 via BleepingComputer; Shadowserver; CISA KEV

items.title: Citrix fixes 31 NetScaler flaws, nine critical, plus a NetScaler Console auth bypass — one critical bug affects default configurations, and there is no workaround
items.content_text: Citrix’s 12 November bulletin fixes 31 vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway. Nine are critical, led by CVE-2026-107412 (CVSS v4 9.5) and CVE-2026-120868 (9.3), which affects default configurations, plus CVE-2026-107407, -107408, -107409, -107410 and -107415 (9.3 each). NetScaler Console has a separate authentication bypass, CVE-2026-120869 (9.4). Fixed releases are ADC/Gateway 14.1-73.57 and 13.1-64.39, FIPS 14.1-73.58 and Console 14.1-74.34. No exploitation has been reported and Citrix lists no workaround. NetScaler has had several exploited critical flaws this year, so plan this as an emergency change.

items.title: Fortinet patches eight critical FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer flaws, including an unauthenticated JSON-RPC code-execution bug — none exploited yet
items.content_text: Fortinet’s November release fixes eight critical flaws. The most serious is CVE-2026-126170 (CVSS 9.8), unauthenticated code execution through the JSON-RPC API, which is off by default. Others cover OFTP SQL injection (CVE-2026-126262) and SSRF (CVE-2026-126229, -126260), the FGFM management protocol (CVE-2026-126261), high availability (CVE-2026-126259), BGP (CVE-2026-126254) and OSPF (CVE-2026-126253). Fixed FortiOS releases are 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.8 and 8.0.2. No exploitation has been reported and none of these flaws is in KEV, but firewalls are prime targets, so schedule the upgrade now rather than waiting for the first exploitation report.

items.title: SAP’s November patch day fixes four CVSS 10.0 flaws, including “ICM2SHELL” and “PROXYGATE”, that Onapsis says allow pre-auth full compromise
items.content_text: SAP released 35 security notes on 10 November, four of them rated the maximum CVSS 10.0: CVE-2026-76964 (“ICM2SHELL” in the NetWeaver AS ABAP Internet Communication Manager), CVE-2026-89126 (ICM2SHELL in SAP Web Dispatcher), CVE-2026-89103 (“PROXYGATE”, a pre-auth RCE in SAP Gateway) and CVE-2026-120017 (missing authorisation in the SAML2 service provider). Onapsis says they can allow full compromise without authentication. No exploitation has been reported. A separate, older SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal flaw did enter KEV on 20 November (see that card), a reminder that attackers do work through SAP backlogs.

items.title: Unpatched Windows “SignDrop” CLFS zero-day gives SYSTEM on Windows 11 26H2 and Server 2025 — public PoC, no CVE, no patch
items.content_text: A researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse has published a proof of concept for “SignDrop”, a local privilege escalation in the Windows Common Log File System driver that gives an attacker SYSTEM rights and bypasses the CLFS mitigation Microsoft added in October 2025. It was tested on Windows 11 26H2 and Windows Server 2025. There is no CVE and no patch yet, and no use in real attacks has been reported. A working SYSTEM exploit turns any user-level foothold into full control of the machine, so watch this closely until Microsoft ships a fix.

items.title: FortiSIEM 7.5.0 flaw CVE-2026-106173 has a public PoC; Singapore’s CSA updated its alert on 20 November and still reports no confirmed exploitation
items.content_text: CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS 9.8) affects FortiSIEM 7.5.0 and is fixed in 7.5.1. A public proof of concept exists. Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency updated its alert on 20 November, the new development this card reflects, and still describes no confirmed exploitation. Earlier editions of this page carried reports of exploitation; the CSA’s current alert does not confirm them, so this card now treats it as a PoC-stage flaw. A SIEM holds credentials for much of the network, so it is worth fixing quickly anyway.

items.title: Legal protections for sharing cyber threat information with the US government expire on 11 December unless Congress renews the 2015 law
items.content_text: The liability and antitrust protections in the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act of 2015 expire on 11 December unless they are renewed. In a 1 November letter, 35 groups including the US Chamber of Commerce, BSA, the American Bankers Association and the American Public Power Association asked negotiators on the defence authorisation bill (NDAA) to keep the House’s 10-year extension to 2035. The sticking point in the Senate is an amendment from Senator Rand Paul. A lapse could make companies more cautious about sharing indicators with government.

items.title: Operation Endgame takes down Gootloader, StealC and CastleRAT infrastructure: 235 servers and 257 domains seized and about 6.4 million victim datasets recovered
items.content_text: Police in nine countries, under the Operation Endgame banner, took down infrastructure for the Gootloader loader, which spreads through infected WordPress sites that pose as legal documents and agreement templates, and for the StealC infostealer and CastleRAT. They seized 235 servers and 257 domains and recovered about 6.4 million victim datasets, including more than 6 million credentials. The RCMP built a removal tool and about 672 infected sites have been cleaned. No arrests were announced. Because the lures pose as legal templates, law firms and the people searching for contracts are natural targets.

items.title: Acting CISA director’s memo narrows FY2027 support toward “systemically important” organisations as the agency operates with about a third fewer staff; a nominee faces holds
items.content_text: A 2 November memo from acting CISA director Nick Andersen sets three FY2027 priorities, national cyber defence, key infrastructure security and nationwide resilience, and focuses the agency’s direct support on systemically important organisations. CISA has lost about a third of its staff. Separately, Palantir CISO Michael LoSapio, nominated on 9 November to lead CISA, declined at his 19 November hearing to comment on layoffs or a proposed $385 million cut, offering a “gap analysis” instead; Senators Tillis and Wyden plan holds, and Andersen remains acting director. Smaller organisations, including many hospitals, schools, nonprofits and local governments, should plan as if direct CISA help will be harder to get.

_threatfeed.date_note: Memo 2 Nov 2026; reported 11 Nov 2026; hearing 19 Nov 2026

items.title: A run of outages, including an FAA ground stop, Outlook and Exchange Online and three days of disruption to NSA’s internal network, has officials saying no cyberattack and lawmakers asking about patching pace
items.content_text: Recent outages include a nationwide FAA ground stop on 13 November, a global Microsoft Outlook and Exchange Online outage, banking slowdowns that Chase traced to a software bug in on-premises hardware on 16 November, and about three days of disruption to NSANet, the NSA’s internal classified network. The Director of National Intelligence tied the NSANet problem to PHP-related patching, and the DNI, DHS and FBI say there is no evidence of a cyberattack. Some lawmakers point to the pace of patching vulnerabilities found by AI tools as a cause; that has not been confirmed. None of these outages has been attributed to attackers.

items.title: A Kazakh national accused of running the “8-Digits Team” behind INC and Lynx ransomware attacks on schools and hospitals has been extradited to the US
items.content_text: Roman Khlynovskiy, 43, of Kazakhstan, was extradited from Italy and appeared in court in Knoxville, Tennessee. Prosecutors allege he ran the “8-Digits Team”, which carried out INC and Lynx ransomware attacks, often against schools and hospitals, in at least six states, demanding $500 million in total. The group claimed to have stolen 50 TB, including more than 70 million health records. He faces up to 27 years. These are allegations, not findings.
